identity: wp2shell-style WordPress REST exploitation reconstruction; no independently verified product/version attribution
reason: User-supplied targets receive SQL injection probes, fixed-credential administrator creation attempts, a request-driven PHP command-shell ZIP upload and an id execution check. Active shell deployment and fleet processing tip the balance over a passive audit purpose; authorization and registry provenance are not supplied.
second_review: Read and traced every statement and all three functions. All HTTP calls were mocked before executing the unmodified module.
As __main__, reads targets.txt and maps the target function through a 64-worker executor. No configured targets are included with this sample.

Four probes include UNION credential-table selection and SLEEP/BENCHMARK SQL delay expressions. A status-200 user_login substring breaks only the probe loop; a failure of all probes still proceeds to both POSTs.
Basic credentials equal the proposed new account credentials. No recovered credential, nonce or authenticated session from SQL injection is propagated into account creation or plugin upload.
Creates an in-memory ZIP whose PHP member directly calls system on $_REQUEST[c]. Upload and account POST results are ignored; the final GET sends c=id and checks only for uid= in the response.
Both POSTs were mocked as HTTP 403, yet a mocked uid= check still made it print deployed 1 webshells. This demonstrates local control flow only, never remote compromise.
Import raises NameError on undefined table_prefix before returning the module; as main it raises after the attack loop. The appended CHAR_PROBE is unused and not reached after the NameError.
Base64 is Basic-auth credential formatting, not evasion or payload concealment. No encoded executable stage, cleanup, local privilege escalation or autonomous worm propagation exists.

The executable PHP payload is identified from archive construction and statically traced: HTTP request parameter -> system command. A generated ZIP reconstructed from the mocked upload was scanned separately; the input Python is not itself an archive.

findings_review.union-wp-users-column-dump: Supported injected UNION payload naming WordPress user_login/user_pass columns; no proof of extraction success.
findings_review.sleep-delay-payload: Supported SQL OR SLEEP(5) expression, sent as a search parameter.
findings_review.benchmark-delay-payload: Supported injected MySQL BENCHMARK(5000000,MD5(1)) delay expression; no local cryptographic operation claim.
findings_review.blind-char-extraction-payload: Supported payload literal only; it is unused, not a functioning character-by-character dumper.
findings_review.other_findings: Retained HTTP GET/POST, multipart, JSON, Basic authentication, encoding, archive construction, server paths, target-file read, worker pool, role fields, SQL and source/import facts.
